chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'A man has committed a wrong against me; should I pardon him or refer him to the ruler?' He said: 'It is your right. If you pardon him, it is good; and if you refer him to the Imam, you are merely seeking your right. And how can you refer him to the Imam?'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on forgiving a wrongdoer versus referring them to the Imam or ruler?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the distinction between *afw* (personal pardon/virtue) and *raf’ ila al-imam* (referencing the Imam for justice), affirming that both are valid but serve different spiritual and legal purposes. The rhetorical question 'How can you [do so] with the Imam?' underscores the unique authority of the Imam in adjudicating rights, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the Imam’s role in enforcing *hudud* and *qisas*. This reflects the Shia view that while individuals may forgive debts or injuries, the full realization of justice often requires the Imam’s jurisdiction, especially in cases involving public rights or specific legal penalties.
